A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cooperative uncertainty-disentanglement method. The complete main texts and Appendices A–F are readable, including equations, tables, and figures, permitting comparison despite extensive renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on synthetic, UCI, image-regression, and simulated material-plasticity datasets, including repeated experiments and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds APPA-REAL experiments, multimodal-noise predictions, calibration analyses, and additional ablations and comparisons.

M1.justification: The three-stage BNN-VE algorithm is retained under the name VeBNN. v2 adds an MDN-based extension producing mode means and mixture weights with an adapted variance network (Appendix D.1, Figure 14), and an optional schedule that iterates ME/VE training before one Bayesian stage (Appendix A.3). The corrected Gamma-loss formula does not establish that its implementation changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds apparent-age regression on APPA-REAL and a synthetic scenario with bimodal heteroscedastic noise. The eight UCI and eight image-regression tasks remain. The separate higher-noise material-plasticity evaluation in v1 Appendix D.3.2 disappears, although both material definitions remain in Appendix F.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated MVE (Natural) baselines on UCI, image, and plasticity datasets, plus MVE (Natural/Ensembles) and MVE (Natural/MC-Dropout) plasticity comparisons. Ensembles enter the illustrative comparison, while MC-Dropout results disappear from the image tables. BNN-End-to-End becoming MVE for BBB/pSGLD is a rename, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix C replaces the image evaluation's 90% conformal intervals with variance-scaling calibration targeting 95%, also applying calibration to UCI. Image reporting changes from MAE and validation intervals to RMSE, TLL, test coverage, and test interval length; plasticity gains coverage, interval-length, and calibration metrics. Appendix E.1 also changes the illustrative experiment's stated K from 5 to 2.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled Gamma-versus-Gaussian and Gamma-versus-beta-NLL/natural-loss ablations, epistemic calibration diagnostics, ensemble loss sensitivity, and Energy-dataset initialization/iteration tests. The existing variance-network-size and plasticity iteration studies are retained in the appendix. Conversely, v1's higher-noise material robustness analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v2 introduces Wilcoxon significance testing for overall and within-inference comparisons, with p<0.05 annotations, and explicitly identifies table dispersions as standard deviations. The existing 20 UCI random splits and five synthetic/plasticity repetitions remain; the PDFs do not establish an increase in these run counts.

E6.justification: Numerous reported results change: proposed-method Concrete RMSE changes from 4.65±0.97 in v1 Table 1 to 4.70±0.77 in v2 Table 6. v2 adds APPA-REAL results, including VeBNN RMSE 17.72 and WA 13.50, alongside new comparator, calibration, and ablation entries, while removing the higher-noise plasticity results. Changed calibration and metrics prevent interpreting revised image scores as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 corrects residual standardization and the Gamma NLL and derivatives, and explicitly states an asymptotic Gamma lemma. Appendix A adds a Hessian-based convexity analysis and a finite-sample bias theorem with iterative-improvement arguments. These substantially extend the mathematics, although the new derivation does not establish its claimed general bias-reduction guarantee.

C1.justification: The central claims about cooperative training, uncertainty disentanglement, scalability, and improved mean estimation remain. v2 explicitly characterizes its demonstration as empirical and removes v1's conclusion that the method does not require validation data.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of ensemble overconfidence, pSGLD failures under strong distribution shift, optimization behavior, computational costs, and limitations of fixed probabilistic assumptions. Its main image discussion now warns about aleatoric inflation under shift, whereas Appendix D.3 retains the claim that VeBNN's aleatoric uncertainty remains stable, leaving an interpretive inconsistency.

D1.justification: Most architecture and optimizer details remain. v2 adds an explicit code-repository link, CPU/GPU specifications, per-stage timings, and APPA-REAL splits, resolution, and annotation counts. Its new description of 100 repeated plasticity simulations is not reconciled with Appendix F's retained description of 50 SVEs, so an actual sampling increase is unclear.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around Bayesian posterior quality, ensemble disentanglement, natural-loss comparisons, alternative uncertainty metrics, and credal learning, citing works including Valdenegro-Toro and Mori, Fishkov, Caprio, and Wang. Skafte becoming Detlefsen and the Mucsányi venue update refer to retained works rather than new research.

P1.justification: The methodology and discussion are extensively rewritten, experiments are reorganized around known versus unknown aleatoric uncertainty, and the illustrative evaluation moves to Appendix D. Appendix A receives a new explanatory structure, while the title and method terminology change throughout.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a grid to a horizontal workflow, prediction panels are rearranged, and plasticity performance plots expand from three to five metrics. The large image-results table becomes separate metric tables, with new comparison markings. Additional ablation, calibration, and multimodal displays substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects v1's erroneous Gamma objective and improves empirical scrutiny through targeted loss ablations, additional baselines, calibration checks, and APPA-REAL's repeated age labels. Code-access and resource disclosures also improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removing the higher-noise plasticity test and introducing weaknesses: Theorem A.1 replaces expected squared estimation error with squared bias, omitting estimator variance, while Section 4.1 and Appendix D.3 disagree about aleatoric behavior under shift. The net improvement is therefore limited.
